title: usages
summary: Finds usage sites of a named symbol, with a choice of report width
intro: Read this when you want every place a symbol is used: usages (also behind Find Usages in the IDE) lists the grouped usage sites of a named symbol, with a narrow, wide or very-wide report width.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint usages --name <X> [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file>] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
help: drag-lint usages             --name <X> [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file>] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
grouped usage report; backs the IDE Symbol Search dialog's Usages view.
--limit N keeps the first N rows of each JSON group (declarations included) and adds
"limit" and "totals" (the full counts); without it nothing is capped.

--rw: the users of a member split into readers and writers, one block per declaration: a property with its backing field and accessor methods, a field with its properties, a getter (reads) or setter (writes). Rows name the route (property, field, getter, setter, direct).

With no --db, --in <file> finds the unit's project and its database. No DB: prints the index command, exits 2. Two projects list it: names both, exits 2. No project: a library unit on an assumed platform, unless it uses units the library lacks (names them, exits 2). With neither --db nor --in the verb exits 2.

steps: Put the caret on the symbol in the editor

questions.ask: How do I get a wider or JSON report?
